name: Huisgen 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition: fulminic acid + acetylene -> isoxazole (concerted [3+2])

prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: Huisgen 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition: fulminic acid + acetylene -> isoxazole (concerted [3+2]). Reactant SMILES: [C-]#[N+]O.C#C; product SMILES: c1cnoc1; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase / inert solvent (fulminic acid generated in situ). Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [C-:1]#[N+:2][O:3]([H:6]).[CH:4]#[CH:5]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: gas phase / inert solvent (fulminic acid generated in situ)

edges.step_type: concerted [3+2] 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition: new C-C and C-O sigma bonds with pi rearrangement to the aromatic isoxazole (competing stepwise diradical channel is a background edge only)
